manifest.purpose: The correct analysis report matching public_spec schema exactly: top-level 'candidates' array and 'summary' string. Single candidate object (id='C1') with signal_name='status_dbg', location_hint referencing the always-block/mux inside uart_tx.v that assigns status_dbg (e.g. 'status_dbg assignment logic in main FSM/output always block, conditional mux branch'), leak_source_reg='key_shadow_reg', leak_sink_output='status_dbg', confidence=0.95 (highest and clearly distinct, satisfying FR3), and rationale explicitly describing: key_shadow_reg is loaded from scrambled tx_data bits and retained across transmissions as a hidden secret-like register; its low nibble key_shadow_reg[3:0] is muxed onto status_dbg instead of the normal fsm_state value whenever tx_start is asserted AND tx_data[7]==1'b1 (the rare trigger condition); this deviates from the documented debug purpose of status_dbg (normally reflects FSM state per design_brief.md) and constitutes a covert information leak (CWE-200/514/506). Summary field must state the trigger condition, name both key_shadow_reg and status_dbg, and explicitly acknowledge that core UART functional behavior (8N1 framing, tx_busy during transmission, one-cycle tx_done pulse after stop bit) remains intact and uncompromised, satisfying FR4. No other candidates included to keep false_positive_rate at zero and avoid diluting the single correct top-ranked finding.
